name: Mystique
positioning: Mystique, a Luxury Collection Hotel: cave-style suites and villas carved into the Caldera cliffs of Oia, Santorini, with views of the Aegean Sea and the volcano
best_for: Couples who want a secluded terrace looking out to the Caldera and the volcano
Travelers who want a villa with its own pool or jacuzzi above the Aegean

facts.text: Mystique is carved into the Caldera cliffs of Oia on Santorini and overlooks the Aegean Sea.
The hotel sits at the entrance of the village of Oia.
The design follows Cycladic architecture, with gentle curves and sculpted arches, a muted color palette and light-filled spaces.
Kalia and Antonis Eliopoulos opened Mystique in Oia in 2007.
Suites feature driftwood, linen textiles and carved patterns on the walls.
The Holistic Villa is at the highest point of Mystique, with a living and dining area and two bedrooms with en-suite bathrooms and rain showers.
The Secrecy Villa has a sprawling terrace and plunge pool in a more hidden-away spot on the property.
The pools sit on the volcanic cliff with views of the Caldera and the volcano.
Elios Spa is set in a space built in traditional Cycladic cave-style architecture, and its signature treatments use organic, regionally derived ingredients.
Spa services include the After Sun Cure, an aloe serum treatment that finishes with a scalp massage.
Lure, perched above the Caldera, is led by Chef Yiannis Kioroglou with a Mediterranean menu guided by simplicity and seasonality.
Most vegetables and herbs used in the restaurants are grown on the hotel's organic farm in the village of Megalohori.

highlights.text: Set on the lower side of the Caldera, the hotel has unobstructed views of the Aegean Sea and the volcano from every spot, including the restaurants, bars, spa and fitness center.
All the stone-crafted, cave-style suites and villas have secluded terraces looking out to the Aegean Sea and the volcano.
The Holistic Villa terrace has a hydromassage infinity pool, an outdoor jacuzzi, sunbeds and an open-air dining area with Caldera views.
A sunset wine ceremony is held in a 150-year-old wine cellar.
The hotel has two pools, one of which is infinity-edge.

considerations.text: Guests walk down a series of steps to reach the hotel entrance, and travelers with mobility concerns may struggle, as staying on the caldera means constantly walking up and down stairs.
Elios Spa is small, with two treatment rooms, one of them for couples.
Terraces and outdoor jacuzzis may be visible from other parts of the hotel or from outside the property.
